title: AI 420 · Module 1 · Lecture Part 2: The Four Components, in About 60 Lines

lines: This is AI 420, Module 1, Lecture Part 2: the four components of an agent, in about sixty lines of code.
The course description names four components.
Reasoning: deciding the next move.
Planning: working out the steps.
Tool use: acting on the outside world.
And memory: keeping track of what's already happened.
In Google's Agent Development Kit, ADK for short, an agent is only a few lines.
The instruction steers its reasoning: look facts up, do every sum with the calculator, and say so if no tool confirms a fact.
The tools list is tool use: two Wikipedia tools and a calculator.
Here's one question, as it appears in ADK's Events tab.
The model doesn't answer yet. It asks for a function call: search Wikipedia for the Space Needle.
ADK runs the tool, and the result comes back as an observation: completed in 1962.
Two more rounds follow, the iPhone, then the calculator. Only then does the model answer in text: 45 years.
So where are the other two components?
Memory is the session. ADK sends every earlier event back to the model on each call, because the model itself remembers nothing.
Planning is the one you can't see. Here, it happens one step at a time, inside each model call. In Week 2, plan-and-execute turns the plan into a list you can inspect.
There's one more thing the model reads: each tool's description.
ADK builds it from the function's name, its type hints, and its docstring. That's all the model sees when it chooses a tool.
Three common mistakes.
A tool with no docstring. The model sees only a name and argument types, so it guesses when to call it.
Running adk web from the wrong folder. Run it from the folder above your agent's folder, or the agent list is empty.
And no step budget. A confused model can call tools again and again, and every call costs tokens. Set a limit on model calls in the run config.
A quick check before you move on.
Remove the step budget. What's the worst case, and who pays for it?
Next, in Part 3: agentic patterns, and the framework you'll build with all term.
